import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Computability.Encoding

/-!
# Kronecker coefficient

The Kronecker coefficient is defined below from irreducible symmetric-group characters, with the
characters given explicitly by the Murnaghan--Nakayama rule. The open problem asks for a positive
combinatorial formula for these coefficients. Its standard complexity-theoretic formulation says
that the function is in `#P` when partitions are encoded by the binary specifications of their
parts.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
- [Ikenmeyer, Mulmuley and Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955)
-/

namespace KroneckerCoefficient

open Computability

/-- Two cells are edge-adjacent in the integer grid. -/
def GridAdjacent (a b : ℕ × ℕ) : Prop :=
  (a.1 = b.1 ∧ (a.2 + 1 = b.2 ∨ b.2 + 1 = a.2)) ∨
    (a.2 = b.2 ∧ (a.1 + 1 = b.1 ∨ b.1 + 1 = a.1))

/-- The cells carrying a given label in a labelled Young diagram. -/
def labelCells {μ : YoungDiagram} {k : ℕ} (T : μ.cells → Fin k) (i : Fin k) :
    Finset μ.cells :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun c ↦ T c = i

/-- A labelled Young diagram is a border-strip tableau of content `ρ`.

Labels describe successive removals starting with label zero. Thus, before every removal, the
cells which have not yet been removed must form a Young diagram. Every label class has its
prescribed cardinality, is edge-connected, and contains no two-by-two square. -/
def IsBorderStripTableau (μ : YoungDiagram) (ρ : List ℕ)
    (T : μ.cells → Fin ρ.length) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Fin (ρ.length + 1), ∀ c : μ.cells, i.val ≤ (T c).val →
    ∀ d : μ.cells, d.val.1 ≤ c.val.1 → d.val.2 ≤ c.val.2 → i.val ≤ (T d).val) ∧
  (∀ i : Fin ρ.length, (labelCells T i).card = ρ[i]) ∧
  (∀ i : Fin ρ.length, ∀ c ∈ labelCells T i, ∀ d ∈ labelCells T i,
    Relation.ReflTransGen
      (fun x y : μ.cells ↦ x ∈ labelCells T i ∧ y ∈ labelCells T i ∧
        GridAdjacent x.val y.val) c d) ∧
  (∀ i : Fin ρ.length, ¬ ∃ r c : ℕ,
    (r, c) ∈ (labelCells T i).image Subtype.val ∧
    (r + 1, c) ∈ (labelCells T i).image Subtype.val ∧
    (r, c + 1) ∈ (labelCells T i).image Subtype.val ∧
    (r + 1, c + 1) ∈ (labelCells T i).image Subtype.val)

/-- The height of a label class, namely one less than its number of occupied rows. -/
def labelHeight {μ : YoungDiagram} {k : ℕ} (T : μ.cells → Fin k) (i : Fin k) : ℕ :=
  ((labelCells T i).image fun c ↦ c.val.1).card - 1

/-- The irreducible symmetric-group character indexed by `μ`, defined by the
Murnaghan--Nakayama rule. -/
noncomputable def character (μ : YoungDiagram) (ρ : List ℕ) : ℤ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ T : μ.cells → Fin ρ.length,
    if IsBorderStripTableau μ ρ T then ∏ i, (-1 : ℤ) ^ labelHeight T i else 0

/-- The Kronecker coefficient, defined by the character formula
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}
\chi^\lambda(\sigma)\chi^\mu(\sigma)\chi^\nu(\sigma)$ when the three diagrams have the same
cardinality, and as zero otherwise. -/
noncomputable def kroneckerCoefficient (la mu nu : YoungDiagram) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact if la.card = mu.card ∧ la.card = nu.card then
    Int.toNat ((∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin la.card),
      character la (σ.partition.parts.sort (· ≤ ·)) *
      character mu (σ.partition.parts.sort (· ≤ ·)) *
      character nu (σ.partition.parts.sort (· ≤ ·))) / la.card.factorial)
  else 0

/-- The bit length of the binary specification of the positive row lengths of a partition. -/
def binarySize (μ : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  (μ.rowLens.map fun n ↦ (encodeNat n).length).sum

/-- A self-delimiting binary code for one positive integer. -/
def selfDelimitingNatCode (n : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  List.replicate (encodeNat n).length true ++ false :: encodeNat n

/-- A self-delimiting binary code for a partition, obtained from its row lengths. -/
def partitionCode (μ : YoungDiagram) : List Bool :=
  μ.rowLens.flatMap selfDelimitingNatCode ++ [false]

/-- The input supplied to the Boolean verifier: three binary partition codes followed by the
certificate bits. -/
def verifierInput (la mu nu : YoungDiagram) (certificate : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  partitionCode la ++ partitionCode mu ++ partitionCode nu ++ certificate

/-- **Combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients (GCT6 conjecture).**

There are a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time computable Boolean function $F$ such that, for
every three partitions $\lambda,\mu,\nu$, the Kronecker coefficient (taken to be zero unless the
three partitions have equal size) is the number of bit strings of length
$p(\langle\lambda\rangle,\langle\mu\rangle,\langle\nu\rangle)$ accepted by $F$. Here
$\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the total bit length of the binary specifications of the parts of
$\lambda$. Equivalently, the binary-encoded Kronecker coefficient function is in `#P`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ p : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℕ, ∃ F : List Bool → Bool,
      Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBool finEncodingBoolBool F) ∧
      ∀ la mu nu : YoungDiagram,
        kroneckerCoefficient la mu nu =
          ∑ certificate :
              Fin (MvPolynomial.eval ![binarySize la, binarySize mu, binarySize nu] p) → Bool,
            (F (verifierInput la mu nu (List.ofFn certificate))).toNat := by
  sorry

end KroneckerCoefficient
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “give a combinatorial interpretation” by the standard complexity-theoretic GCT6 formulation cited in Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter: the binary-encoded Kronecker coefficient function belongs to #P.
Represented integer partitions by Mathlib YoungDiagram values and measured input size as the sum of the binary bit-lengths of their positive row lengths, rather than using the weaker unary encoding.

Defined irreducible symmetric-group character values by the Murnaghan–Nakayama signed border-strip-tableau formula because Mathlib has no Specht modules or partition-indexed irreducible-character API.
Used Equiv.Perm.partition.parts, rather than Equiv.Perm.cycleType, when evaluating characters; the former includes the 1-cycles (fixed points) required by the character formula.
Defined the Kronecker coefficient as zero when the three diagram cardinalities differ, and otherwise by the standard normalized character sum over the symmetric group.
Used a multivariate polynomial over ℕ evaluated at the three binary specification lengths for the exact certificate length.

Presented the polynomial-time verifier as a Boolean function on one self-delimiting packed bit string and required Mathlib's TM2ComputableInPolyTime with the existing List Bool encoding. The delimiters add only linear overhead to the cited binary representation.

import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.Millenium.PvsNP

/-!
# Kronecker coefficient

The Kronecker coefficients $g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ are the multiplicities in the decomposition
$V_\mu \otimes V_\nu = \bigoplus_\lambda g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} V_\lambda$ of the tensor product of
two irreducible representations (Specht modules) of the symmetric group $S_n$. Equivalently,
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
  \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma) \chi^\nu(\sigma),$$
where $\chi^\lambda$ is the character of $V_\lambda$.

A major open problem, posed by Murnaghan in 1938, is to give a combinatorial interpretation
of the Kronecker coefficients. Following Ikenmeyer, Mulmuley and Walter, the formal
complexity-theoretic version of this problem is the conjecture (from Mulmuley's GCT6) that the
Kronecker coefficients have a $\#P$-formula, i.e. that the map
$(\lambda, \mu, \nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ lies in the counting class $\#P$ when the
partitions are given in binary.

Mathlib has no Specht modules, so we construct the irreducible representation $V_\lambda$ of
$S_n$ as the left ideal of the group algebra $\mathbb{Q}[S_n]$ generated by the Young
symmetrizer $c_T = a_T b_T$ of a tableau $T$ of shape $\lambda$, as in Fulton–Harris, and
$\chi^\lambda$ as its character. The choice of the tableau does not affect $\chi^\lambda$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [C. Ikenmeyer, K. D. Mulmuley, M. Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*,
  Comput. Complexity 26 (2017), 949–992](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955), §1.3 and §2.3
- [K. D. Mulmuley, *Geometric complexity theory VI: The flip via positivity*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0229)
- W. Fulton, J. Harris, *Representation theory. A first course*, §4.2
-/

open Computability Equiv Finset MonoidAlgebra

namespace KroneckerCoefficient

variable {n : ℕ}

/- ### Irreducible characters of the symmetric group

A tableau with `n` entries is a map `T : Fin n → ℕ × ℕ` assigning a cell to each entry. -/

/-- The row group of a tableau `T`: the permutations of the entries that keep every entry in
its row. -/
def rowGroup (T : Fin n → ℕ × ℕ) : Finset (Perm (Fin n)) :=
  {σ | ∀ k, (T (σ k)).1 = (T k).1}

/-- The column group of a tableau `T`: the permutations of the entries that keep every entry in
its column. -/
def colGroup (T : Fin n → ℕ × ℕ) : Finset (Perm (Fin n)) :=
  {σ | ∀ k, (T (σ k)).2 = (T k).2}

/-- The Young symmetrizer $c_T = a_T b_T$ of a tableau `T` in the group algebra
$\mathbb{Q}[S_n]$, where $a_T = \sum_{\sigma \in P_T} \sigma$ is the sum over the row group and
$b_T = \sum_{\sigma \in Q_T} \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma) \sigma$ is the signed sum over the
column group. -/
noncomputable def youngSymmetrizer (T : Fin n → ℕ × ℕ) : MonoidAlgebra ℚ (Perm (Fin n)) :=
  (∑ σ ∈ rowGroup T, single σ 1) *
    ∑ σ ∈ colGroup T, single σ ((Perm.sign σ : ℤ) : ℚ)

/-- The left ideal $\mathbb{Q}[S_n] c_T$ of the group algebra generated by the Young
symmetrizer of `T`. When `T` is a bijection onto the cells of a Young diagram $\lambda$ with `n`
cells, this is the irreducible representation $V_\lambda$ of $S_n$ (the Specht module), acted
on by left multiplication. -/
noncomputable def spechtModule (T : Fin n → ℕ × ℕ) :
    Submodule ℚ (MonoidAlgebra ℚ (Perm (Fin n))) :=
  LinearMap.range (LinearMap.mulRight ℚ (youngSymmetrizer T))

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mul_mem_spechtModule (T : Fin n → ℕ × ℕ) (x : MonoidAlgebra ℚ (Perm (Fin n)))
    {y : MonoidAlgebra ℚ (Perm (Fin n))} (hy : y ∈ spechtModule T) :
    x * y ∈ spechtModule T := by
  obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := hy
  exact ⟨x * z, by simp [mul_assoc]⟩

/-- The action of `σ ∈ Sₙ` on `spechtModule T` by left multiplication. -/
noncomputable def spechtAction (T : Fin n → ℕ × ℕ) (σ : Perm (Fin n)) :
    spechtModule T →ₗ[ℚ] spechtModule T :=
  (LinearMap.mulLeft ℚ (single σ (1 : ℚ))).restrict fun _ hy => mul_mem_spechtModule T _ hy

/-- A tableau of shape `μ` with `n = |μ|` entries: a bijection from `Fin n` onto the cells of
`μ`. Any bijection gives an isomorphic representation, so the character below does not depend on
this choice. -/
noncomputable def tableau (μ : YoungDiagram) (hμ : μ.card = n) : Fin n → ℕ × ℕ :=
  fun k => (Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq ((Fintype.card_coe μ.cells).trans hμ)).symm k

/-- The irreducible character $\chi^\mu$ of $S_n$ indexed by the partition `μ` of `n`: the
character of the Specht module $V_\mu$, i.e. `character μ hμ σ` is the trace of the action of
`σ` on $V_\mu$. -/
noncomputable def character (μ : YoungDiagram) (hμ : μ.card = n) (σ : Perm (Fin n)) : ℚ :=
  LinearMap.trace ℚ _ (spechtAction (tableau μ hμ) σ)

/-- The Kronecker coefficient
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
  \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma) \chi^\nu(\sigma)$$
of three partitions `lam`, `μ`, `ν` of the same integer `n`, i.e. the multiplicity of
$V_\lambda$ in $V_\mu \otimes V_\nu$. It is `0` if the partitions do not have the same size. -/
noncomputable def kroneckerCoefficient (lam μ ν : YoungDiagram) : ℚ :=
  if h : μ.card = lam.card ∧ ν.card = lam.card then
    (lam.card.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹ * ∑ σ : Perm (Fin lam.card),
      character lam rfl σ * character μ h.1 σ * character ν h.2 σ
  else 0

@[category API, AMS 5 20]
theorem kroneckerCoefficient_eq_zero {lam μ ν : YoungDiagram}
    (h : ¬ (μ.card = lam.card ∧ ν.card = lam.card)) : kroneckerCoefficient lam μ ν = 0 := by
  simp [kroneckerCoefficient, h]

/-- The one-row partition `(n)` indexes the trivial character. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem character_eq_one_of_rowLens_eq {μ : YoungDiagram} (hμ : μ.card = n)
    (h : μ.rowLens = [n]) (σ : Perm (Fin n)) : character μ hμ σ = 1 := by
  sorry

/-- The Kronecker coefficient of three empty partitions (the trivial representation of the
trivial group $S_0$) is `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 20]
theorem kroneckerCoefficient_bot : kroneckerCoefficient ⊥ ⊥ ⊥ = 1 := by
  sorry

/- ### Binary encodings

The input to a $\#P$-formula is a triple of partitions, each given in binary, together with a
bit string. We encode it as a single bit string. -/

/-- The bit-length $\langle \mu \rangle$ of a partition: the total number of binary digits of
its parts. -/
def bitLength (μ : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  (μ.rowLens.map Nat.size).sum

/-- A self-delimiting binary encoding of a list of natural numbers as a bit string: every binary
digit `b` of a number (least significant digit first) is written as the two bits `true, b`, and
every number is terminated by the bit `false`. -/
def encodeNatList (l : List ℕ) : List Bool :=
  l.flatMap fun k => (Nat.bits k).flatMap (fun b => [true, b]) ++ [false]

/-- The binary encoding of the input `(lam, μ, ν, σ)` of a $\#P$-formula: the parts of the three
partitions in binary, each list of parts terminated by the separator `0` (which is not a part
since parts are positive), followed by the bit string `σ`. Its length is linear in
$\langle \lambda \rangle + \langle \mu \rangle + \langle \nu \rangle + |\sigma|$. -/
def encodeInput (lam μ ν : YoungDiagram) (σ : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  encodeNatList (lam.rowLens ++ 0 :: μ.rowLens ++ 0 :: ν.rowLens ++ [0]) ++ σ

@[category API, AMS 68]
theorem encodeInput_injective :
    Function.Injective fun x : YoungDiagram × YoungDiagram × YoungDiagram × List Bool =>
      encodeInput x.1 x.2.1 x.2.2.1 x.2.2.2 := by
  sorry

@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem encodeNatList_example :
    encodeNatList [2, 0] = [true, false, true, true, false, false] := by
  have h2 : Nat.bits 2 = [false, true] := by
    rw [show (2 : ℕ) = 2 * 1 from rfl, Nat.bit0_bits _ one_ne_zero, Nat.one_bits]
  simp [encodeNatList, h2]

/- ### The conjecture -/

/-- **Kronecker coefficients have a combinatorial interpretation.**

Murnaghan (1938) asked for a combinatorial description of the Kronecker coefficients
$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$. The formal complexity-theoretic version of this problem, conjectured in
Mulmuley's GCT6 and recorded by Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, is that the Kronecker coefficients
have a $\#P$-formula: there are a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time computable $0$-$1$
function $F$ such that for all partitions $\lambda, \mu, \nu$
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma),$$
where $\langle \lambda \rangle$ is the total bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$ written in
binary. In other words, the map $(\lambda, \mu, \nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$, with the
partitions given in binary, is in $\#P$.

Here `F` is a function on bit strings, computable in polynomial time by a Turing machine, and
the input `(lam, μ, ν, σ)` is passed to it via the binary encoding `encodeInput`; the polynomial
`p` is evaluated at $\langle\lambda\rangle + \langle\mu\rangle + \langle\nu\rangle$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (F : List Bool → Bool),
      ComplexityTheory.IsComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBool finEncodingBoolBool F ∧
      ∀ lam μ ν : YoungDiagram,
        kroneckerCoefficient lam μ ν =
          #{σ : Fin (p.eval (bitLength lam + bitLength μ + bitLength ν)) → Bool |
            F (encodeInput lam μ ν (List.ofFn σ))} := by
  sorry

end KroneckerCoefficient
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table's single slot and its notes (binary input, g := 0 off the diagonal, define g via characters since Mathlib lacks Specht modules, exclude the known hardness theorems) were followed.
modeling_decisions: The Wikipedia entry ('give a combinatorial interpretation') is informal; following the decomposition table and IMW §1.3, the formal statement is the GCT6 conjecture that (λ,μ,ν) ↦ g^λ_{μν} is in #P, with the partitions encoded in binary (the unary version would be weaker and is not stated).

Kronecker coefficient defined as (1/n!) Σ_{σ∈S_n} χ^λ(σ)χ^μ(σ)χ^ν(σ) in ℚ (Wikipedia's formula), and set to 0 when |λ|,|μ|,|ν| are not all equal. The conjecture compares this rational with the cast of a natural-number count.

χ^λ is the character of the irreducible representation V_λ constructed à la Fulton–Harris §4.2: the left ideal ℚ[S_n]·c_T generated by the Young symmetrizer c_T = a_T b_T of a tableau T of shape λ, acted on by left multiplication; the character is LinearMap.trace over ℚ. Working over ℚ instead of ℂ is harmless (S_n-characters are rational). The tableau is any bijection Fin n ≃ λ.cells, taken as Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq; the character is independent of this choice (standard fact, stated in docstrings but not proved). With this construction the one-row partition indexes the trivial character and the one-column partition the sign character, matching the Specht-module labeling.
Partitions are Mathlib `YoungDiagram`s (size `card`, parts `rowLens`); the parameter n is carried as a hypothesis `μ.card = n` so all three characters live on Perm (Fin n).

#P membership is spelled out directly (no #P class exists in the repo): p : Polynomial ℕ (a genuine polynomial, as in the standard definition of #P; the paper's phrase 'polynomially-bounded function' is read this way), evaluated at ⟨λ⟩+⟨μ⟩+⟨ν⟩ where ⟨λ⟩ = Σ Nat.size(parts) is the total binary bit-length. A single-variable polynomial in the sum is equivalent to a polynomial in the three bit-lengths.
Witnesses σ ∈ {0,1}^{p(...)} are modeled as `Fin (p.eval …) → Bool`, converted to a bit string with List.ofFn; the sum of the 0-1 function is the Finset card of the σ with F = true.

F : List Bool → Bool is a single Turing-machine-computable function on bit strings: polynomial time is `ComplexityTheory.IsComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBool finEncodingBoolBool F` (Mathlib's TM2ComputableInPolyTime, same convention as the repo's P and NP), imported from FormalConjectures.Millenium.PvsNP (other Wikipedia files import problem files similarly). The tuple (λ,μ,ν,σ) is passed to F via the explicit injective binary encoding `encodeInput`: parts written in binary via a self-delimiting scheme (each bit b as `true,b`, terminator `false`), the three part-lists separated by the non-part 0, then σ appended. Any polynomially inter-convertible binary encoding yields an equivalent statement; the encoding length is linear in ⟨λ⟩+⟨μ⟩+⟨ν⟩+|σ|.
Known theorems mentioned in the article (#P-hardness, GapP membership, NP-hardness of positivity) are not posed as questions and are not stated.

Added sorry'd sanity tests (one-row partition gives the trivial character; g(∅,∅,∅)=1; encodeInput injective) alongside two proved API/test lemmas; precedent for unproved test lemmas exists in the Wikipedia folder.

import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.Millenium.PvsNP

/-!
# Kronecker coefficient

The Kronecker coefficients $g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ describe the decomposition of the tensor product
of two irreducible representations of the symmetric group $S_n$ into irreducible representations:
$V_\mu \otimes V_\nu = \bigoplus_\lambda g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} V_\lambda$. They can be computed as
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
  \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma) \chi^\nu(\sigma),$$
where $\chi^\lambda$ is the irreducible character of $S_n$ indexed by the partition $\lambda$ of
$n$.

A major unsolved problem, open since Murnaghan asked it in 1938, is to give a combinatorial
interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients. Its standard formal, complexity-theoretic version
(conjectured by Mulmuley in GCT6, see Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, Section 1.3) asks for a
$\#P$-formula: a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ such that
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma),$$
where $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the total bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$ written in binary.

Mathlib has no Specht modules, so the irreducible characters of $S_n$ are defined here through
Frobenius' character formula: $\chi^\lambda(\sigma)$ is the coefficient of the monomial
$x^{\lambda + \delta}$, with $\delta = (n - 1, n - 2, \dots, 0)$, in
$\prod_{i < j} (x_i - x_j) \cdot \prod_k p_{\rho_k}(x)$, where $\rho$ is the cycle type of
$\sigma$ and $p_k$ is the $k$-th power sum in the variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [C. Ikenmeyer, K. D. Mulmuley, M. Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*,
  Computational Complexity 26 (2017)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955)
- [K. D. Mulmuley, *Geometric Complexity Theory VI: the flip via positivity*,
  Technical report, University of Chicago (2010)](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0229)
-/

open Computability MvPolynomial Equiv

namespace KroneckerCoefficient

/-- The `i`-th largest part of the partition `μ` (indexing from `0`), or `0` if `μ` has at most
`i` parts. -/
def part {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).getD i 0

/-- The Vandermonde product $\prod_{i < j} (x_i - x_j)$ in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. -/
noncomputable def vandermonde (n : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  ∏ i, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (X i - X j)

/-- The value $\chi^\lambda(\sigma)$ of the irreducible character of $S_n$ indexed by the
partition $\lambda$ of $n$ at the permutation $\sigma$, given by Frobenius' character formula:
the coefficient of the monomial $x^{\lambda + \delta}$, $\delta = (n - 1, n - 2, \dots, 0)$, in
$\prod_{i < j} (x_i - x_j) \cdot \prod_k p_{\rho_k}$, where $\rho$ is the cycle type of
$\sigma$ (including the fixed points as parts equal to $1$) and $p_k = \sum_i x_i^k$. -/
noncomputable def character {n : ℕ} (lam : n.Partition) (σ : Perm (Fin n)) : ℤ :=
  coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin n => part lam i + (n - 1 - i))
    (vandermonde n * psumPart (Fin n) ℤ σ.partition)

/-- The Kronecker coefficient
$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma)
\chi^\nu(\sigma)$ of three partitions $\lambda, \mu, \nu$ of $n$. -/
noncomputable def kroneckerCoeff {n : ℕ} (lam μ ν : n.Partition) : ℚ :=
  (n.factorial : ℚ)⁻¹ *
    ∑ σ : Perm (Fin n), (character lam σ * character μ σ * character ν σ : ℚ)

/-- The trivial character: $\chi^{(n)}(\sigma) = 1$ for all $\sigma \in S_n$. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 20]
theorem character_indiscrete {n : ℕ} (σ : Perm (Fin n)) :
    character (Nat.Partition.indiscrete n) σ = 1 := by
  sorry

@[category test, AMS 5 20]
theorem character_zero (lam : Nat.Partition 0) (σ : Perm (Fin 0)) : character lam σ = 1 := by
  simp only [character, vandermonde, psumPart, Perm.partition, Subsingleton.elim σ 1]
  rw [Subsingleton.elim (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm _) 0]
  simp

@[category test, AMS 5 20]
theorem kroneckerCoeff_zero (lam μ ν : Nat.Partition 0) : kroneckerCoeff lam μ ν = 1 := by
  simp [kroneckerCoeff, character_zero]

/-- The binary encoding of a partition as a bit string. The parts are listed in decreasing
order. Each part is written in binary (least significant digit first) with every binary digit `d`
written as the pair `[true, d = 1]`; each part is terminated by the pair `[false, false]`, and the
whole partition is terminated by the pair `[false, true]`. The encoding of a partition $\lambda$
with $\ell$ parts has length $2\langle\lambda\rangle + 2\ell + 2$, where
$\langle\lambda\rangle \ge \ell$ is the total bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$. -/
def encodePartition {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  (μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).flatMap
    (fun a => (Nat.digits 2 a).flatMap (fun d => [true, decide (d = 1)]) ++ [false, false]) ++
    [false, true]

/-- The binary encoding of a triple of partitions of `n`, obtained by concatenating the
encodings of the three partitions. -/
def encodeTriple {n : ℕ} (lam μ ν : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  encodePartition lam ++ encodePartition μ ++ encodePartition ν

@[category test, AMS 5 68]
theorem encodePartition_indiscrete_three :
    encodePartition (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 3) =
      [true, true, true, true, false, false, false, true] := by
  simp [encodePartition, Nat.Partition.indiscrete, Nat.Partition.ofSums, Multiset.filter_singleton,
    Multiset.sort_singleton]

@[category test, AMS 5 68]
theorem encodePartition_indiscrete_six :
    encodePartition (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 6) =
      [true, false, true, true, true, true, false, false, false, true] := by
  norm_num [encodePartition, Nat.Partition.indiscrete, Nat.Partition.ofSums,
    Multiset.filter_singleton, Multiset.sort_singleton]

/-- The unary encoding of a partition as a bit string. The parts are listed in decreasing order,
each part `a` is written as `a` copies of `true` followed by `false`, and the whole partition is
terminated by another `false`. The encoding of a partition of `n` with `ℓ` parts has length
`n + ℓ + 1`. -/
def unaryEncodePartition {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  (μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).flatMap (fun a => List.replicate a true ++ [false]) ++ [false]

/-- The unary encoding of a triple of partitions of `n`, obtained by concatenating the
encodings of the three partitions. -/
def unaryEncodeTriple {n : ℕ} (lam μ ν : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  unaryEncodePartition lam ++ unaryEncodePartition μ ++ unaryEncodePartition ν

@[category test, AMS 5 68]
theorem unaryEncodePartition_indiscrete_three :
    unaryEncodePartition (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 3) = [true, true, true, false, false] := by
  simp [unaryEncodePartition, Nat.Partition.indiscrete, Nat.Partition.ofSums,
    Multiset.filter_singleton, Multiset.sort_singleton, List.replicate]

/--
**Combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients** (Murnaghan, 1938), in the formal
version of Mulmuley (GCT6) recorded by Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter: the Kronecker coefficients
have a $\#P$-formula. That is, there exist a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time computable
$0$-$1$ function $F$ such that for every $n$ and all partitions $\lambda, \mu, \nu$ of $n$,
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma),$$
where the partitions are specified in binary and $\langle\lambda\rangle$ denotes the total
bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$.

Here the triple $(\lambda, \mu, \nu)$ is given to $F$ as the bit string `encodeTriple lam μ ν`,
whose length is linear in $\langle\lambda\rangle + \langle\mu\rangle + \langle\nu\rangle$, and
$F$ is computed by a polynomial-time Turing machine taking as input the pair (instance, witness)
of bit strings, as in `ComplexityTheory.NP`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool),
      ComplexityTheory.IsComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool
        finEncodingBoolBool F ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (lam μ ν : n.Partition),
        kroneckerCoeff lam μ ν =
          Fintype.card {σ : Fin (p.eval (encodeTriple lam μ ν).length) → Bool //
            F (encodeTriple lam μ ν, List.ofFn σ) = true} := by
  sorry

/--
The weaker, unary version of `kronecker_coefficient`: the Kronecker coefficients have a
$\#P$-formula when the partitions are specified in unary, i.e. there exist a polynomial $p$ and a
polynomial-time computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ such that for every $n$ and all partitions
$\lambda, \mu, \nu$ of $n$,
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(n)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma).$$
This is the version of the problem that corresponds most directly to counting combinatorial
objects of size polynomial in $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient.variants.unary :
    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool),
      ComplexityTheory.IsComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool
        finEncodingBoolBool F ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (lam μ ν : n.Partition),
        kroneckerCoeff lam μ ν =
          Fintype.card {σ : Fin (p.eval (unaryEncodeTriple lam μ ν).length) → Bool //
            F (unaryEncodeTriple lam μ ν, List.ofFn σ) = true} := by
  sorry

end KroneckerCoefficient

modeling_decisions: The informal 'give a combinatorial interpretation' is formalized as the standard complexity-theoretic version recorded in the cited paper (§1.3) and conjectured in GCT6: the map (λ,μ,ν) ↦ g^λ_{μν} has a #P-formula, i.e. ∃ p, F with g = Σ_{σ∈{0,1}^{p(...)}} F(λ,μ,ν,σ), F a poly-time 0-1 function.

This is a theorem-turned-definition; sign/index conventions were checked by hand on S_2 and S_3 (trivial, sign and standard characters and the resulting Kronecker coefficients). kroneckerCoeff is ℚ-valued, literally (1/n!)·Σ, and compared with the (cast) natural number of accepting witnesses; no integer division or toNat is used.

Only triples of partitions of the same n are considered (via the type Nat.Partition n), matching Wikipedia's formula; the paper's convention g=0 for unequal sizes is equivalent for #P membership since the size check is polynomial-time.

Input encoding: the main theorem uses a binary encoding (paper's definition; ⟨λ⟩ = total bit-length of parts). The encoding is injective (pairwise self-delimiting parsing; Nat.digits is injective), but injectivity is not proved in Lean.

The paper's 'polynomially-bounded function p' is taken to be a Polynomial ℕ evaluated at the encoding length, as in the classical definition of #P and the repository's ComplexityTheory.NP; witnesses have length exactly p(|enc|).

Poly-time computability of F is expressed with the repository's ComplexityTheory.IsComputableInPolyTime (Mathlib's TM2ComputableInPolyTime) on List Bool × List Bool → Bool via finEncodingListBoolProdListBool, imported from FormalConjectures.Millenium.PvsNP (importing another problem file has precedent in Wikipedia/HappyEndingProblem.lean).

import Mathlib.Computability.TMComputable
import Mathlib.GroupTheory.Perm.Cycle.Type

/-!
# Kronecker coefficients

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
- [Ikenmeyer, Mulmuley and Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*]
  (https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955)
-/

open scoped BigOperators
open Computability

namespace KroneckerCoefficient

noncomputable section

/-- The number of boxes of a Young diagram. -/
def partitionSize (la : YoungDiagram) : ℕ := la.cells.card

/-- The exponent $\lambda+\delta$ in the Frobenius coefficient formula, with the rows of
$\lambda$ padded by zeroes. -/
def frobeniusExponent (la : YoungDiagram) : Fin (partitionSize la) →₀ ℕ :=
  Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i ↦
    la.rowLens.getD i 0 + (partitionSize la - 1 - i)

/-- The Vandermonde polynomial $\prod_{i<j}(x_i-x_j)$. -/
def vandermonde (n : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.X j)

/-- The product of power sums associated to a cycle type. Here the cycle type includes its
parts of size one. -/
def powerSumProduct (n : ℕ) (ρ : Multiset ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  (ρ.map fun k ↦ ∑ i : Fin n, MvPolynomial.X i ^ k).prod

/-- The irreducible character of the symmetric group indexed by `la`, defined by the Frobenius
coefficient formula. The multiset `ρ` is the full cycle type, including 1-cycles. -/
def irreducibleCharacter (la : YoungDiagram) (ρ : Multiset ℕ) : ℤ :=
  (vandermonde (partitionSize la) * powerSumProduct (partitionSize la) ρ).coeff
    (frobeniusExponent la)

/-- The full cycle type of a permutation, including its fixed points. -/
def fullCycleType {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Multiset ℕ :=
  σ.cycleType + Multiset.replicate (n - σ.support.card) 1

/-- The Kronecker coefficient, extended by zero when the three partitions do not have the same
size. -/
def kroneckerCoefficient (la μ ν : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  if partitionSize μ = partitionSize la ∧ partitionSize ν = partitionSize la then
    Int.toNat
      ((∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (partitionSize la)),
          irreducibleCharacter la (fullCycleType σ) *
            irreducibleCharacter μ (fullCycleType σ) *
              irreducibleCharacter ν (fullCycleType σ)) / (partitionSize la).factorial)
  else 0

/-- A self-delimiting binary encoding of one natural number. -/
def encodeNat (n : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  List.replicate n.bits.length true ++ false :: n.bits

/-- A binary encoding of a partition: first encode the number of rows, then every row length. -/
def encodePartition (la : YoungDiagram) : List Bool :=
  encodeNat la.rowLens.length ++ la.rowLens.flatMap encodeNat

/-- A binary encoding of a triple of partitions. -/
def encodeTriple (la μ ν : YoungDiagram) : List Bool :=
  encodePartition la ++ encodePartition μ ++ encodePartition ν

/-- The total bit-length of the positive row lengths specifying a partition in binary. -/
def binaryLength (la : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  (la.rowLens.map Nat.size).sum

/-- Evaluation of a three-variable polynomial at the binary lengths of three partitions. -/
def witnessLength (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℕ) (la μ ν : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  MvPolynomial.eval (fun i ↦ ![binaryLength la, binaryLength μ, binaryLength ν] i) p

/--

complexity-theoretic form asks for a positive $\#P$ formula: there are a polynomial $p$ and a
polynomial-time computable Boolean function $F$ such that, for every three partitions
$\lambda,\mu,\nu$, the Kronecker coefficient (defined to be zero unless their sizes agree) equals
$$
  \sum_{s\in\{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle,\langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda,\mu,\nu,s).
$$
Here $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the total binary bit-length of its row lengths. The verifier receives
self-delimiting binary encodings of the three partitions and the witness string.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℕ) (F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool),
      Nonempty
        (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool finEncodingBoolBool F) ∧
      ∀ la μ ν : YoungDiagram,
        kroneckerCoefficient la μ ν =
          ∑ s : Fin (witnessLength p la μ ν) → Bool,
            (F (encodeTriple la μ ν, List.ofFn s)).toNat := by
  sorry

end

end KroneckerCoefficient

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kronecker coefficients

The Kronecker coefficients $g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ describe the decomposition of the tensor
product of two irreducible representations of the symmetric group $S_n$ into irreducibles:
$V_\mu \otimes V_\nu = \bigoplus_\lambda g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} V_\lambda$. Equivalently,
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
  \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma) \chi^\nu(\sigma),$$
where $\chi^\lambda$ is the character of the irreducible representation of $S_n$ indexed by
the partition $\lambda$ of $n$.

Murnaghan (1938) asked for a combinatorial description of the Kronecker coefficients, i.e. a
positive combinatorial rule "akin to" the Littlewood–Richardson rule. The problem is still
open. Its standard formal, complexity-theoretic version (Mulmuley, GCT6; see also
Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, §1.3) is the conjecture that the map
$(\lambda, \mu, \nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ is in the counting class $\#P$: there is a
polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ such that
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma),$$
where $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the bit length of $\lambda$ written in binary.

## Implementation notes

* Mathlib has no Specht modules, so the character $\chi^\lambda$ is defined by the Frobenius
  character formula (Fulton–Harris, Theorem 4.10): for $\sigma$ of cycle type
  $\rho = (\rho_1, \rho_2, \dots)$ (including the $1$-cycles),
  $\chi^\lambda(\sigma)$ is the coefficient of $x_1^{\lambda_1 + n - 1} x_2^{\lambda_2 + n - 2}
  \cdots x_n^{\lambda_n}$ in $\prod_{i < j} (x_i - x_j) \cdot \prod_k p_{\rho_k}(x)$, where
  $p_k(x) = \sum_i x_i^k$ and $\lambda$ is padded with zeros to length $n$.
* The Kronecker coefficient is defined as a rational number by the character formula above; it
  is in fact a natural number.
* Partitions are encoded in binary as bit strings (`encodeBinary`); a weaker variant uses unary
  encoding (`encodeUnary`), as for the positivity problem of Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* C. Ikenmeyer, K. D. Mulmuley, M. Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*,
  Comput. Complexity 26 (2017), [arXiv:1507.02955](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955), §1.3.
* K. D. Mulmuley, *Geometric Complexity Theory VI: the flip via positivity*, Technical report,
  Computer Science Department, University of Chicago (2010);
  [arXiv:0704.0229](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0229).
* P. Bürgisser, C. Ikenmeyer, *The complexity of computing Kronecker coefficients*,
  FPSAC 2008 (the coefficients are $\#P$-hard to compute and lie in GapP).
* F. D. Murnaghan, *The analysis of the direct product of irreducible representations of the
  symmetric groups*, Amer. J. Math. 60 (1938).
* W. Fulton, J. Harris, *Representation Theory: A First Course*, Springer GTM 129, §4.3.
* R. P. Stanley, *Positivity problems and conjectures in algebraic combinatorics*, Problem 10.
-/

namespace KroneckerCoefficient

open Computability Equiv Finset MvPolynomial

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The parts of a partition `μ` of `n`, listed in decreasing order. -/
def sortedParts (μ : n.Partition) : List ℕ := μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)

/-- The `i`-th part `μᵢ` of a partition `μ` (indexed from `0`, in decreasing order), which is
`0` when `i` is at least the number of parts. -/
def part (μ : n.Partition) (i : ℕ) : ℕ := (sortedParts μ).getD i 0

/-- The Vandermonde product $\prod_{i < j} (x_i - x_j)$ in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. -/
noncomputable def vandermonde (n : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, ∏ j ∈ Ioi i, (X i - X j)

/-- The character $\chi^\lambda(\sigma)$ of the irreducible representation of $S_n$ indexed by
the partition $\lambda$ of $n$, evaluated at $\sigma \in S_n$, given by the Frobenius character
formula: it is the coefficient of the monomial
$x_0^{\lambda_1 + n - 1} x_1^{\lambda_2 + n - 2} \cdots x_{n-1}^{\lambda_n}$
in $\prod_{i < j} (x_i - x_j) \cdot \prod_{k} p_{\rho_k}(x)$, where $\rho = (\rho_1, \rho_2, \dots)$
is the cycle type of $\sigma$ (including its fixed points as $1$-cycles) and
$p_k(x) = \sum_i x_i^k$. -/
noncomputable def character (lam : n.Partition) (σ : Perm (Fin n)) : ℤ :=
  coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin n => part lam i + (n - 1 - i))
    (vandermonde n * psumPart (Fin n) ℤ σ.partition)

/-- The Kronecker coefficient
$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma)
\chi^\nu(\sigma)$, the multiplicity of the irreducible representation $V_\lambda$ of $S_n$ in
$V_\mu \otimes V_\nu$. It is a natural number, here regarded as a rational number. -/
noncomputable def kroneckerCoeff (lam μ ν : n.Partition) : ℚ :=
  (∑ σ : Perm (Fin n), character lam σ * character μ σ * character ν σ) / n.factorial

/-- The trivial representation is indexed by the one-part partition $(n)$: its character
is identically $1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 20]
theorem character_indiscrete (σ : Perm (Fin n)) :
    character (Nat.Partition.indiscrete n) σ = 1 := by
  sorry

/-- Tensoring with the trivial representation does nothing: $g^{(n)}_{\mu\nu} = \delta_{\mu\nu}$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 20]
theorem kroneckerCoeff_indiscrete (μ ν : n.Partition) :
    kroneckerCoeff (Nat.Partition.indiscrete n) μ ν = if μ = ν then 1 else 0 := by
  sorry

/-- A self-delimiting binary encoding of a natural number `k`: each bit `b` of the binary
expansion `Computability.encodeNat k` is written as the two bits `[true, b]`, and the whole
is terminated by `false`. -/
def encodeNatDelim (k : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (encodeNat k).flatMap (fun b => [true, b]) ++ [false]

/-- The binary encoding of a partition `μ` of `n` as a bit string: the number of parts, followed
by the parts in decreasing order, each written with `encodeNatDelim`. Its length is linear in
the total bit length $\langle\mu\rangle$ of the parts written in binary. -/
def encodeBinary (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  encodeNatDelim (Multiset.card μ.parts) ++ (sortedParts μ).flatMap encodeNatDelim

/-- The unary encoding of a partition `μ` of `n` as a bit string: the parts in decreasing order,
each part `k` written as `k` copies of `true` followed by `false`. Its length is at most `2 * n`. -/
def encodeUnary (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  (sortedParts μ).flatMap fun k => unaryEncodeNat k ++ [false]

/-- The counting class $\#P$: the set of functions `f : List Bool → ℕ` for which there are a
polynomial `p` and a polynomial-time computable `F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool` such that
`f x` is the number of witnesses `w ∈ {0,1}^{p(|x|)}` with `F (x, w) = true`, for every `x`. -/
def SharpP : Set (List Bool → ℕ) :=
  { f | ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool),
      Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool
        finEncodingBoolBool F) ∧
      ∀ x, f x = #{w : Fin (p.eval x.length) → Bool | F (x, List.ofFn w)} }

/--
**Combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients** (Murnaghan 1938; GCT6 conjecture).

Give a combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients $g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$.
In its standard formal version (Mulmuley, GCT6; Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, §1.3), this asks
for a $\#P$-formula: the function $(\lambda, \mu, \nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$, with the
partitions $\lambda, \mu, \nu$ of $n$ given in binary, is in $\#P$. That is, there are a
polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ such that
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma)$$
for all partitions $\lambda, \mu, \nu$ of the same $n$, where $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the bit
length of $\lambda$ written in binary.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ f ∈ SharpP, ∀ (n : ℕ) (lam μ ν : n.Partition),
      kroneckerCoeff lam μ ν = f (encodeBinary lam ++ encodeBinary μ ++ encodeBinary ν) := by
  sorry

/--
The weaker form of the conjecture in which the partitions $\lambda, \mu, \nu$ are given in unary,
so that the witness length and the running time of $F$ may be polynomial in
$n = |\lambda| = |\mu| = |\nu|$: the function $(\lambda, \mu, \nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$,
with partitions encoded in unary, is in $\#P$. This is implied by `kronecker_coefficient`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient.variants.unary :
    ∃ f ∈ SharpP, ∀ (n : ℕ) (lam μ ν : n.Partition),
      kroneckerCoeff lam μ ν = f (encodeUnary lam ++ encodeUnary μ ++ encodeUnary ν) := by
  sorry

end KroneckerCoefficient

Characters χ^λ of S_n are defined by the Frobenius character formula: coefficient of x_0^{λ_1+n-1}⋯x_{n-1}^{λ_n} in ∏_{i<j}(x_i - x_j)·∏_k p_{ρ_k}(x), where ρ = cycle type of σ including 1-cycles (Mathlib's `Equiv.Perm.partition`, whose parts include the fixed points, is used with `MvPolynomial.psumPart`). This is a theorem-equivalent definition, not the Specht-module definition; the sign convention ∏_{i<j}(x_i - x_j) was hand-checked against the S_2 and S_3 character tables (e.g. χ^{(2,1)} = 2, 0, −1 on identity, transposition, 3-cycle).
Parts of a `Nat.Partition n` are indexed via `Multiset.sort (· ≥ ·)` (decreasing order) with `getD i 0` padding by zeros to length n, as the Frobenius formula requires.

The Kronecker coefficient is defined as a rational number (integer character sum divided by n! in ℚ); it is integer-valued mathematically. The conjecture equates it with the ℕ-valued #P function via coercion.

#P is defined on string functions `List Bool → ℕ`: ∃ polynomial p : Polynomial ℕ and F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool, poly-time via `Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool finEncodingBoolBool` (mirroring the repo's NP definition in Millenium/PvsNP.lean, which cannot be imported by a problem file), with f x = #{w ∈ {0,1}^{p(|x|)} | F (x, w)}. The paper's 'polynomially bounded function of the three bit lengths' is modeled as a polynomial in the total input length; witness strings have exactly length p(|x|), the standard Valiant definition.

Binary input encoding: a partition is encoded as the number of parts followed by the parts in decreasing order, each natural number in self-delimiting binary (each bit b of Mathlib's `Computability.encodeNat` written as [true, b], terminated by false); the triple is the concatenation. The #P function is only required to agree with g on encodings of triples of partitions of the same n (where g is defined); its values elsewhere are unconstrained. This is equivalent to the 'take g = 0 otherwise' convention, since validity of the input is poly-time checkable.

The Kronecker coefficients $g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ are the multiplicities in the decomposition of a
tensor product of two irreducible representations of the symmetric group $S_n$ into irreducible
representations: $V_\mu \otimes V_\nu = \bigoplus_\lambda g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} V_\lambda$.
They can be computed from the irreducible characters $\chi^\lambda$ of $S_n$ by
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
  \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma) \chi^\nu(\sigma).$$

The Wikipedia list of unsolved problems asks to "give a combinatorial interpretation of the
Kronecker coefficients" (a question of Murnaghan, 1938). The standard formal version of this
problem, recorded as a conjecture in Mulmuley's GCT6 and stated as such by
Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, is that the Kronecker coefficients have a `#P`-formula: the map
$(\lambda, \mu, \nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ is in the counting class `#P`, where the
partitions are given in binary.

partitions, so this file defines $\chi^\lambda$ through the Frobenius character formula: for
$\sigma \in S_n$ of cycle type $\rho$ (fixed points counted as $1$-cycles), $\chi^\lambda(\sigma)$
is the coefficient of $x_1^{\lambda_1 + n - 1} x_2^{\lambda_2 + n - 2} \cdots x_n^{\lambda_n}$ in
$$\prod_{1 \le i < j \le n} (x_i - x_j) \cdot \prod_k p_{\rho_k}(x_1, \dots, x_n),$$

The open problem of finding a positive combinatorial rule for the Kronecker coefficients is
formalized as the standard complexity-theoretic conjecture that they admit a `#P` formula.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
- [Ikenmeyer, Mulmuley and Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955)
-/

namespace KroneckerCoefficient

open scoped BigOperators
open Computability Turing

/-- The grid graph on cells: two cells are adjacent when they share an edge. -/
def cellGraph : SimpleGraph (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun a b ↦
    (a.1 = b.1 ∧ (a.2 + 1 = b.2 ∨ b.2 + 1 = a.2)) ∨
    (a.2 = b.2 ∧ (a.1 + 1 = b.1 ∨ b.1 + 1 = a.1))

/-- A finite set of cells is a border strip if it is edge-connected and contains no square of four
cells. -/
def IsBorderStrip (s : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) : Prop :=
  (cellGraph.induce (s : Set (ℕ × ℕ))).Connected ∧
    ∀ i j : ℕ, ¬ ((i, j) ∈ s ∧ (i + 1, j) ∈ s ∧
      (i, j + 1) ∈ s ∧ (i + 1, j + 1) ∈ s)

/-- The height of a finite set of cells is the number of rows that it meets. -/
def stripHeight (s : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) : ℕ :=
  (s.image Prod.fst).card

/-- Cells of `μ` assigned the removal step `i`. -/
def removedAt {k : ℕ} (μ : YoungDiagram) (t : μ.cells → Fin k) (i : Fin k) :
    Finset (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  (μ.cells.attach.filter fun c ↦ t c = i).map ⟨Subtype.val, Subtype.val_injective⟩

/-- Cells of `μ` still present immediately before removal step `i`. -/
def remainingAt {k : ℕ} (μ : YoungDiagram) (t : μ.cells → Fin k) (i : Fin k) :
    Finset (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  (μ.cells.attach.filter fun c ↦ i ≤ t c).map ⟨Subtype.val, Subtype.val_injective⟩

/-- `t` describes a Murnaghan--Nakayama removal of border strips whose sizes are `parts`.
The lower-set condition says that the cells remaining before every step form a Young diagram. -/
def IsRemovalTableau (μ : YoungDiagram) (parts : List ℕ)
    (t : μ.cells → Fin parts.length) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Fin parts.length,
    (∀ c ∈ remainingAt μ t i, ∀ d ≤ c, d ∈ remainingAt μ t i) ∧
    IsBorderStrip (removedAt μ t i) ∧
    (removedAt μ t i).card = parts[i]

/-- The irreducible symmetric-group character indexed by `μ`, defined by the
Murnaghan--Nakayama rule. Fixed points are included among the parts of `σ.partition`. -/
noncomputable def irreducibleCharacter {n : ℕ} (μ : YoungDiagram) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℤ := by
  classical
  exact let parts := Multiset.sort σ.partition.parts (· ≥ ·)
  ∑ t : μ.cells → Fin parts.length,
    if IsRemovalTableau μ parts t then
      ∏ i : Fin parts.length, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (stripHeight (removedAt μ t i) - 1)
    else 0

/-- The Kronecker coefficient, defined by the symmetric-group character formula. It is zero unless
all three Young diagrams have the same number of cells. -/
noncomputable def kroneckerCoefficient (lam μ ν : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  if lam.card = μ.card ∧ lam.card = ν.card then
    Int.toNat ((∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin lam.card), irreducibleCharacter lam σ *
      irreducibleCharacter μ σ * irreducibleCharacter ν σ) / lam.card.factorial)
  else 0

/-- A self-delimiting binary code for a bit: its first bit distinguishes data from delimiters. -/
def encodeDataBit : Bool → List Bool
  | false => [false, false]
  | true => [false, true]

/-- A self-delimiting binary code of a Young diagram's positive row lengths. `true, false`
terminates a row and `true, true` terminates the diagram. -/
def binaryCode (μ : YoungDiagram) : List Bool :=
  μ.rowLens.flatMap (fun n ↦ (encodeNat n).flatMap encodeDataBit ++ [true, false]) ++ [true, true]

/-- The bit length used in the witness bound: the sum of the ordinary binary lengths of the row
lengths. -/
def binaryBitLength (μ : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  (μ.rowLens.map fun n ↦ (encodeNat n).length).sum

/-- The canonical packed binary input containing three Young diagrams. -/
def packTriple (lam μ ν : YoungDiagram) : List Bool :=
  binaryCode lam ++ binaryCode μ ++ binaryCode ν

/--
**Combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients.**

The map $(\lambda,\mu,\nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ is in `#P` with the partitions
encoded by the binary representations of their row lengths. Precisely, there are a polynomial
$p$ and one polynomial-time computable Boolean function $F$ such that every Kronecker coefficient
is the number of Boolean strings of length
$p(\langle\lambda\rangle,\langle\mu\rangle,\langle\nu\rangle)$ accepted by $F$.
Here the coefficient is defined to be zero when the three partitions do not have equal size.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℕ) (F : (List Bool × List Bool) → Bool),
      Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool finEncodingBoolBool F) ∧
      ∀ lam μ ν : YoungDiagram,
        kroneckerCoefficient lam μ ν =
          ∑ w : Fin (MvPolynomial.eval ![binaryBitLength lam, binaryBitLength μ,
            binaryBitLength ν] p) → Bool,
            if F (packTriple lam μ ν, List.ofFn w) then 1 else 0 := by
  sorry

end KroneckerCoefficient
modeling_decisions: Interpreted Wikipedia's terse request for a combinatorial interpretation as the standard formal complexity-theoretic conjecture that the Kronecker coefficient function belongs to #P, following the cited Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter formulation.
Used Mathlib's `YoungDiagram` as the partition type and defined the Kronecker coefficient to be zero unless all three diagrams have equal cardinality.

Because Mathlib has generic finite-group characters but no Specht modules, Schur functions, or irreducible symmetric-group representations indexed by partitions, defined the irreducible character faithfully by the Murnaghan–Nakayama border-strip rule and then used the character-average formula for the coefficient.
Included fixed points in permutation cycle data by using all parts of `Equiv.Perm.partition`, rather than only the nontrivial cycles in `cycleType`.

Measured each partition by the sum of the ordinary binary lengths of its positive row lengths, as in the paper. Used a self-delimiting packing of the three row-length lists as the verifier input; this packing has linear overhead over those binary lengths.
Represented the witness-bound polynomial as `MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℕ`, evaluated at the three separate binary bit lengths, and counted Boolean functions of exactly that length.

Required the verifier to be polynomial-time computable using Mathlib's `TM2ComputableInPolyTime` and the repository's encoding of a pair of Boolean lists. The first list is the canonical packed partition triple and the second is the witness.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kronecker coefficients

The Kronecker coefficient is defined below from the Frobenius character formula. This avoids a
choice of models for the irreducible representations of the symmetric group. The open problem of
finding a combinatorial interpretation is stated in its standard complexity-theoretic form: the
Kronecker coefficient function, with partitions encoded in binary, belongs to `#P`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
- [Ikenmeyer, Mulmuley and Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955)
-/

namespace KroneckerCoefficient

open Computability Turing

/-- A self-delimiting binary encoding of a natural number. -/
def encodeNat (n : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  List.replicate n.bits.length true ++ false :: n.bits

/-- The binary encoding of a partition is the concatenation of the self-delimiting binary
encodings of its nonzero row lengths. -/
def encodePartition (la : YoungDiagram) : List Bool :=
  la.rowLens.flatMap encodeNat

/-- Add a self-delimiting length prefix to a bit string. -/
def frame (s : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  List.replicate s.length true ++ false :: s

/-- The input supplied to the verifier: three framed binary partition encodings followed by the
witness bits. -/
def verifierInput (la mu nu : YoungDiagram) {k : ℕ} (w : Fin k → Bool) : List Bool :=
  frame (encodePartition la) ++ frame (encodePartition mu) ++ frame (encodePartition nu) ++
    List.ofFn w

/-- A Boolean function on bit strings is computable in polynomial time if a Mathlib two-tape
Turing machine computes it in a number of steps polynomial in the input length. -/
def IsPolynomialTime (f : List Bool → Bool) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBool finEncodingBoolBool f)

/-- The irreducible character of the symmetric group indexed by `la`, in the concrete form of
Frobenius' alternant formula. The inner count assigns each cycle of `σ` to a row; saying that the
assignment is constant on cycles is expressed by `c (σ x) = c x`. -/
noncomputable def irreducibleCharacter (la : YoungDiagram) {n : ℕ}
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℤ :=
  if la.card = n then
    ∑ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (Equiv.Perm.sign π : ℤ) *
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun c : Fin n → Fin n =>
        (∀ x, c (σ x) = c x) ∧ ∀ i,
          ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => c x = i).card : ℤ) =
            (la.rowLen i : ℤ) + (π i : ℕ) - (i : ℕ)).card : ℤ)
  else 0

/-- The Kronecker coefficient, defined by the character formula
$g^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}
\chi^\lambda(\sigma)\chi^\mu(\sigma)\chi^\nu(\sigma)$ when the three partitions have the same
size, and as zero otherwise. -/
noncomputable def kronecker (la mu nu : YoungDiagram) : ℕ :=
  if la.card = mu.card ∧ la.card = nu.card then
    Int.toNat ((∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin la.card),
      irreducibleCharacter la σ * irreducibleCharacter mu σ * irreducibleCharacter nu σ) /
        la.card.factorial)
  else 0

/--
A precise form of “give a combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients” is the
GCT6 conjecture that the map $(\lambda,\mu,\nu)\mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ is in `#P`, for the
strong binary encoding of partitions. Thus there are a polynomial witness length and a
polynomial-time computable Boolean verifier whose number of accepting witnesses is the
Kronecker coefficient. The coefficient is taken to be zero unless the three partitions have the
same size.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (F : List Bool → Bool), IsPolynomialTime F ∧
      ∀ la mu nu : YoungDiagram,
        kronecker la mu nu =
          ∑ w : Fin (p.eval
            (frame (encodePartition la) ++ frame (encodePartition mu) ++
              frame (encodePartition nu)).length) → Bool,
            if F (verifierInput la mu nu w) then 1 else 0 := by
  sorry

end KroneckerCoefficient
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the terse request for a combinatorial interpretation as the standard GCT6 conjecture that the Kronecker coefficient function has a #P formula, following Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter and the fixed decomposition table.
Used `YoungDiagram` as the type of integer partitions. Its finite list of positive row lengths is encoded in binary with self-delimiting prefixes; the three partition encodings are framed separately.

Used one polynomial in the total framed partition-input length rather than a function displayed with three separate bit-length arguments. These presentations are polynomially equivalent, and the total framed length is linear in the sum of the three binary specification lengths.

Represented the polynomial-time 0-1 verifier as a Boolean function on one self-delimiting bit string containing the three encoded partitions followed by the witness. Polynomial time is Mathlib's `TM2ComputableInPolyTime`.

Defined irreducible symmetric-group characters concretely by Frobenius' alternant formula: a signed count of maps constant on permutation cycles with prescribed fiber sizes. This avoids unavailable Specht modules and does not postulate character values.

Defined the Kronecker coefficient by the normalized sum of three character values, returning zero when the partition sizes differ, as required by the decomposition table. The empty triple consequently has coefficient one.
